correctness.rationale: For k arms with s edges and s-k+2 vertices, a spanning tree must leave exactly one full terminal path and delete one edge on each of the others. Counting terminal/internal leaves gives z^(k-1)[sum_i prod_{j!=i}(2+(ell_j-2)z)+2k(z-1)]/tau, tau=sum_i prod_{j!=i}ell_j. For ell_a=p>=q+2=ell_b+2, balancing changes the numerator by delta*z^2 Q and tau by delta*Q(1), delta=p-q-1. The exact mixture law is old law with weight tau/(tau+delta R) plus H law with weight delta R/(tau+delta R), R=Q(1)>0. Coupling the intact path and keeping shared edge cuts yields H-L=E_a+E_b-J if intact path is in the remainder, or E_b+E_h-J / E_a+E_h-J otherwise; J=1 forces the two indicated cuts to touch the same terminal, hence each difference is nonnegative. Opposite-end cuts give strictness with positive probability, proving stochastic order and strict mean, and majorization reaches the two global extrema. Direct independent deletion-pattern enumeration reproduced exact leaf polynomials for six configurations, including (2,3,5,4); the symbolic coupling, not the finite checks, proves the universal claim. No arbitrary weighted-network/general-series-parallel extension is asserted.

value.rationale: A genuine nontrivial distributional majorization law: it applies to every increasing leaf statistic, not merely expectation, and identifies both extremal subdivisions at fixed cycle rank and edge budget. The explicit mixture-coupling explains a strict stochastic ordering not forced by the spanning-tree count alone.

limitations: All arms must have at least two edges; uniform unweighted spanning trees and fixed number/total length only.
Finite sample counts are corroboration; no extension to arbitrary conductances or arbitrary series-parallel graphs.
